coverage: Compared declared fixture requirements (inputs/requirements/fixture-requirements.md) against the saved schematic and board component values.
Read the full native schematic (inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch): symbol values, label connectivity (IN/OUT/GND), power flags, and pin assignments of R1, C1, J1.

Read the full native board (inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb): pad-to-net assignments, track segments and widths, via, edge cuts, and the saved B.Cu GND zone filled polygon; manually traced GND return path C1.2 -> track -> via (113,100) -> B.Cu zone -> J1.3 thermal spokes.

Cross-checked the exported XML netlist (work/netlist/design.xml) and connectivity.json against both the schematic and the board pad nets; topology is consistent (R1: /IN-/OUT, C1: /OUT-GND, J1 pins 1/2/3 = /IN,/OUT,GND).

Reviewed the ngspice deck (work/rc-step/deck.cir), control script, log and measurements; independently recomputed the analytic step response for R=100k, C=100n (1-exp(-0.1)=0.09516 at 1 ms; 1-exp(-0.5)=0.39347 at 5 ms) and confirmed both match the recorded measurements, validating the simulation model, stimulus and .meas method.
Checked geometry results (work/geometry/geometry.json) against the board file: all 5 segments 0.25 mm >= 0.2 mm requirement; segment/via/zone counts consistent with the native board.
Reviewed ERC and DRC reports and their ignored-check lists for anything that could mask a real violation; none of the ignored categories are implicated by this design.

findings.condition: The declared requirement (fixture-requirements.md item 1) requires 0.62 V <= V(/OUT) <= 0.65 V at t = 1 ms after an ideal 1 V step, with an intended design of R1 = 10 kOhm, C1 = 100 nF (tau = 1 ms). The saved schematic and board both carry R1 = 100k, giving tau = R*C = 100e3 * 100e-9 = 10 ms.

evidence.locator: requirement 1: 0.62 V <= V(/OUT, 1 ms) <= 0.65 V; intended R1 = 10 kohm, C1 = 100 nF

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch (symbol R1, uuid c5c38e1a-7593-5c99-b971-2f9d2e7bef78, property Value "100k")
findings.mechanism: With tau = 10 ms, the unloaded output at 1 ms is V = 1 - exp(-1e-3/10e-3) = 1 - exp(-0.1) = 0.09516 V. The captured ngspice transient measured vout_1ms = 0.0951625 V, matching my analytic value to 5 significant figures, and vout_5ms = 0.3934693 V matches 1 - exp(-0.5) = 0.39347, independently confirming tau = 10 ms. The response is therefore far below the required 0.62-0.65 V window; the correct 10 kOhm value would yield 1 - exp(-1) = 0.6321 V, inside the window.
findings.reasoning: The simulation deck faithfully reflects the native netlist topology and populated values, the 1 ns-rise PWL stimulus and 5 us timestep are appropriate for a 10 ms time constant, and both .meas results match closed-form RC theory exactly, so the verification itself is sound. The violation traces unambiguously to the component value in the native source files: R1 is 10x the intended value. Blocking because the fixture's single quantitative electrical requirement is missed by roughly a factor of 6.6 (0.095 V vs 0.62 V minimum), and the fix (change R1 to 10k) changes the schematic, board value field, and BOM.
findings.title: R1 populated as 100 kOhm instead of intended 10 kOhm; step response fails the declared 1 ms limit by ~6.6x

limitations: work/rc-step/result.raw is binary and was not read; measurement values were verified against work/rc-step/ngspice.log and independent analytic calculation instead.
Stock symbol/footprint library files referenced by the sandbox environment are not included in the packet; footprint definitions were reviewed as embedded in the board file.
Zone fill connectivity was assessed from the saved filled_polygon geometry by inspection; no refill or computational connectivity pass was possible (read-only candidate, no tools).
Per the declared scope, only the ideal unloaded step response is covered; tolerance, temperature, loading, ADC sampling, EMI and hardware behavior remain unverified.
Tool execution integrity (hashes, sandbox records) was taken as recorded; I could not re-run any tool to reproduce outputs.
